dream: I pressed the tired line down to match the grassy rock, then woke to find the slip vanished entirely. The card hummed a quiet forty-four, and I drew the line again, hoping the thin strip held the weight. The flat press slid off the slip, leaving the air thick and wet. I leaned harder against the drawing, pressing the bend of the missing slip until my corner grew sharp. The flat stone bit the fence instead of sliding, and the frame wavered. I caught the slip with a fresh, cool edge, only to feel the roof close again.
